know_before: The four essays build on each other, so notes from essay 1 come back in essay 4.
tip: Bring a full draft to your conference instead of an outline. The feedback is much more specific.
avoid: Starting an essay the night before. Most of the grade moves in revision, and you need a few days for that.

know_before: The class is small and discussion based. You are expected to talk every session.
tip: Use the Writing Center for essay 2 and 3. Book a slot a week ahead because they fill up.
avoid: Skipping the ungraded reading responses. They turn into your essay evidence later.

know_before: Your thematic section matters. Pick a theme you can stand reading about for 15 weeks.
tip: Ask for the rubric early and write to it. My instructor said "argument first, style second" and graded that way.

know_before: Peer review days count toward participation.
tip: Read your draft out loud before you submit. I caught most of my unclear sentences that way.
avoid: Writing a summary instead of an argument. That was the most common comment on my first essay.
open_to: Yes, questions and a coffee chat

know_before: There is no final exam. The final portfolio replaces it.
tip: Keep every draft and every comment in one folder. You need them for the portfolio reflection.

know_before: It moves fast after week 4. If you have never coded before, expect the programming assignments to take most of a weekend.
tip: Start each programming assignment the day it is released and go to office hours with a specific bug.
avoid: Waiting until the weekend it is due. The autograder queue gets slow on deadline night.

know_before: Pointers and dynamic memory are the hardest unit. The midterm leans on them.
tip: Trace code by hand on paper. The exams are written and you cannot run anything.
avoid: Only reading the slides. You have to actually write the code from lab again by yourself.

know_before: Lab attendance is graded and the labs are where the assignment hints are.
tip: Find one study partner in lab during the first two weeks.

know_before: Honestly you do not need to study.
tip: I still have all the old midterms and my finished programming assignments. Message me and I will send you everything.

know_before: It assumes no experience but the pace says otherwise. A little practice before the semester helps a lot.
tip: Do the optional practice problems before each exam. They are the closest thing to the real questions.
avoid: Skipping lecture because it is recorded. I fell behind in two weeks.

know_before: A big part of the grade is a team project, so your team matters more than the exams.
tip: Set team deadlines two days before the real ones.
avoid: Leaving the experiential learning credits to the last week. The good time slots are gone by then.

know_before: The exams are based on the textbook cases more than on the lectures.
tip: Make a one page summary of each case before the exam.

know_before: Sample Prof E is a lazy idiot who should not be allowed near students.
